name: Swell Maps
label: Rough Trade
lede: Solihull teenagers who'd been taping songs in each other's bedrooms since 1972 pressed an 87-second single, got John Peel to play it ten times, and made two albums with vacuum cleaners and balloons on them. Thurston Moore said they had a lot to do with his upbringing.

eras.title: Bedrooms, bikes and the Faust Tapes
eras.text: The Godfrey brothers and their friends spent most of the 1970s making music on cassette in Solihull, outside Birmingham. Punk opened venues and studios to bands like them, and they took the hint fast.

years.src: The Quietus · The Guardian: Swell Maps
years.h: Sunday school in Solihull turns into a bedroom band
years.p: David Barrington met Adrian and Kevin Godfrey at Sunday school in 1969; Adrian's schoolfriend Stephen Bird joins by 1972. They record in each other's bedrooms, taking their cue from Faust's The Faust Tapes.
years.xp: Earlier names included Sacred Mushroom, Xerox and Calico and the Black Riders. Adrian loved T. Rex, Bowie and the Stones; Kevin and Bird went for prog, Gong and krautrock. Bird and Adrian cycled from the Midlands to the south coast together and saw Mott the Hoople and Led Zeppelin.

years.h: Sudden's names for his bandmates: Bondage Pelican, Cleavage Frogdog
years.p: Everyone takes a pseudonym as punk breaks, inspired by Gong more than the Damned. Adrian becomes [[Nikki Sudden|2485c631-fbfb-462d-9ac9-060375040682]], Kevin [[Epic Soundtracks|1fc042ce-4032-408f-99ce-ab698d697c22]], Bird [[Jowe Head|3863fd93-5820-4574-9585-f30d71cfbaa5]], Richard Scaldwell Biggles Books, Barrington Phones Sportsman.

years.src: The Quietus · The Guardian: Swell Maps
years.h: The first studio day, at Spaceward in Cambridge
years.p: Five songs in one session, Read About Seymour among them. Scaldwell says they took the name Swell Maps, from Thunderbirds, just before.
years.xp: Buzzcocks' Spiral Scratch had shown them you could hire a studio and put out your own record. Jowe Head told the Guardian they weren't ready before 1977, and that punk nights let them on stage without a demo tape or covers.

years.src: The Guardian: Nikki Sudden · The Guardian: Swell Maps · Wikipedia: Swell Maps
years.h: Read About Seymour: 87 seconds on their own Rather label
years.p: Sudden brought the song in and said it was about the king of the mods. John Peel played it ten times in twelve shows.
years.xp: The single is named in [[Television Personalities|62c2cd94-30a8-43ed-9d06-8f689111c69c]]' Part Time Punks, and a Guardian editor later picked it as one of 25 classic punk singles.

eras.title: Rough Trade, Peel and a vacuum cleaner
eras.text: Rough Trade gave them a 50/50 deal, Peel gave them three sessions, and a four-track studio in Leamington Spa caught the noise. Two albums and three years later it was over.

years.h: Sudden takes the singles to Geoff Travis, who wants in at once
years.p: Rough Trade agrees a distribution and production deal with a straight 50/50 split, Scaldwell says. The Maps also back Steve Treatment on a Rather EP.
years.xp: Travis saw them as early adopters of the Desperate Bicycles' do-it-yourself credo. In 1979 they backed the Cult Figures on Zip Nolan for Rough Trade.

years.cap: Swell Maps in Anti Climax fanzine, issue 3
years.src: The Quietus: Swell Maps Peel sessions · The Quietus: Organised
years.h: The first of three Peel sessions
years.p: The BBC records the band in October 1978, then in May 1979 and March 1980. Jowe Head calls it mind-blowing.

years.src: The Quietus · Wikipedia: A Trip to Marineville · Wikipedia: Swell Maps
years.h: A vacuum cleaner on Midget Submarines, balloons on Gunboats
years.p: Most of the debut is cut at WMRS in Leamington Spa with John Rivers, December 1978 to April 1979. It reaches No. 10 on the UK indie chart.
years.xp:
Head played the vacuum. He told the Quietus they were used to switching on a cassette machine and doing everything off the cuff, not multi-tracking. Scaldwell called these the best times they had in a studio, though bouncing down on Rivers' four-track cost a lot of definition.

Later in 1979 the single Let's Build a Car reached No. 6 on the indie chart, their biggest. Stereolab's Tim Gane says he played the album a hundred times or more.

years.src: The Quietus · The Guardian: Swell Maps
years.h: In a van through Belgium and Holland with Scritti Politti
years.p: Only four Maps tour: Barrington and John Cockrill don't play live. The band feels closer to [[Scritti Politti|a2588b38-6532-4186-b0c8-9aff306d56f5]], [[The Pop Group|4c9f194e-6235-475a-bf7b-2fd54a0879ec]] and Alternative TV than to the big punk names.

years.cap: Jowe Head and Nikki Sudden at ULU, London, c. February 1980
years.h: A water pistol, a gang of skinheads and Jowe Head in surgery
years.p: Head is badly beaten after squirting skinheads with a water pistol. Gigs are cancelled, and the wound keeps reopening on the next tour.
years.xp: Head told the Guardian in 2026 he felt guilty for something dumb that rebounded on the band: "I was unwell for a considerable period, more than I like to admit." There was no word for PTSD then, he said, but he was badly shaken.

years.src: The Quietus · The Guardian: Swell Maps
years.h: A disastrous Italian tour ends Swell Maps
years.p: Biggles Books told the others so after Italy, where crowds expected something else from the first new wave band through. Epic and Head wouldn't go on without him, and Sudden was devastated.
years.xp:
The band had already drifted: Sudden moved to London expecting the others to follow and go full-time, while Head went to art college in Manchester and Soundtracks in Portsmouth. Barrington saw friction between the members treating it as a job and those treating it as fun.

Only weeks earlier, in March, Geoff Travis had seen them at London's Moonlight Club and called it a magic night. Head's version of the end: they could have taken a couple of months off, "but no, we decided to dramatically split up."

years.src: Wikipedia: Jane from Occupied Europe · The Quietus
years.h: Jane from Occupied Europe comes out after the split
years.p: Recorded mostly at WMRS from June 1979 to May 1980, the second album reaches No. 4 on the UK indie chart. Head hears more restraint and more light and shade on it.

years.cap: Swell Maps in Back Issue fanzine, issue 3, 1980
years.h: Rain, Rain, Rain, and an album lost for 43 years
years.p: Soundtracks and Head put out a Rough Trade single meant to lead into Daga Daga Daga. The album was never finished until Head found the tapes in 2023; it came out in 2024.

eras.title: The spine of indie, and two brothers lost
eras.text: Swell Maps were gone, but the people around them and Television Personalities became the core of Creation Records. In America, the band's records were turning up in the collections of Sonic Youth, Pavement and R.E.M.

years.src: Wikipedia: Swell Maps · The Guardian: Swell Maps · The Quietus
years.h: Thurston Moore writes that the Maps raised him
years.p: In 1981 the future [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] guitarist praises Sudden's guitar and the band's songcraft in print. The archive double Whatever Happens Next... comes out the same year.
years.xp:
[[Pavement|36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3]]'s Scott Kannberg later said the Maps were a big influence on Pavement's early records, great songs buried under mess. Stephen Malkmus has said Pavement started as something like a tribute to them and the Desperate Bicycles.

Scaldwell put out The Egg Store Ilk as Richard Earl in 1981, then left music and became known for restoring vintage cars and motorbikes.

years.h: Jowe Head gets thrown off David Gilmour's tour with the TVPs
years.p: On the opening night, Dan Treacy read out Syd Barrett's address before I Know Where Syd Barrett Lives. Head threw confetti, was sent to sweep the stage, and the band was bundled off the tour.
years.xp: Head spent about a decade in [[Television Personalities|62c2cd94-30a8-43ed-9d06-8f689111c69c]]. Sudden, Soundtracks, Head, Treacy, Ed Ball and Joe Foster formed, as the Guardian put it, the spine of Creation Records through the 1980s.

years.src: Wikipedia: Nikki Sudden · The Guardian: Nikki Sudden
years.h: R.E.M. back Nikki Sudden at Peter Buck's house
years.p: Sudden records The Jewel Thief with [[R.E.M.|ea4dfa26-f633-4da6-a52a-f49ea4897b58]] in Athens, Georgia. He'd already made three albums as The Jacobites with Dave Kusworth.
years.xp: In 2004 his album Treasure Island featured Ian McLagan of the Small Faces and ex-Rolling Stone Mick Taylor, the childhood idols he'd always wanted to play with. Secretly Canadian began reissuing all his solo work in 2002.

years.src: Wikipedia: Epic Soundtracks · Wikipedia: Swell Maps
years.h: Epic Soundtracks steps out from behind the drums with Rise Above
years.p: After drumming for Crime and the City Solution and [[These Immortal Souls|502f5022-ed77-48d9-b92c-b6c73fa9715a]], he becomes a piano balladeer. Sleeping Star (1994) and Change My Life (1996) follow.
years.xp: He'd also drummed for Mayo Thompson's Red Krayola while Swell Maps were still going.

years.cap: Nikki Sudden with Freddy Lynxx at Wild at Heart, Berlin, 1997
years.h: Epic Soundtracks dies in his sleep at 38
years.p: Kevin Godfrey was found at his flat in West Hampstead, London. The official cause of death was ruled inconclusive.

years.cap: Nikki Sudden at the Cake Shop, New York, March 24, 2006
years.src: New York Times · The Guardian: Nikki Sudden · Wikipedia: Nikki Sudden
years.h: Nikki Sudden dies in New York, a day after a Knitting Factory show
years.p: He was 49 and died of a heart attack, according to Wikipedia and the Quietus. He'd left almost 30 albums, solo, with the Jacobites and with Swell Maps.

eras.title: Jowe Head, archivist, starts the band again
eras.text: As the last of the core trio, Head went through the tapes, wrote a book and talked Mute into the Peel sessions. Then he built a new Swell Maps.

years.cap: Jowe Head at the Swell Maps sessions, Cafe Oto, London, December 2021
years.h: Swell Maps C21 plays all six founders' songs
years.p: Head's new line-up settles with Lee McFadden, Jeff Bloom, David Callahan, Lucie Rejchrtova, Luke Haines and Chloe Herington.

years.src: The Quietus: Swell Maps Peel sessions
yt: Let's Buy a Bridge, Peel session, March 1980
years.h: Mute puts out the Peel sessions after more than 40 years
years.p: The John Peel Sessions collects the October 1978, May 1979 and March 1980 sessions, newly remastered.

yt: Swell Maps on the C21 album and lineup
years.h: "Here come the hits!" says Head, 46 years after the last album
years.p: C21 mixes rediscovered and unfinished songs with new ones, on Tiny Global Productions. Phones Sportsman and Golden Cockrill contribute.
